topic: security of LLM-based AI agents: prompt injection, jailbreak, RAG poisoning, tool abuse, MCP and multi-agent security, defenses and benchmarks
scope: Security of LLM-based agents from 2022 onward: how prompt injection (direct and indirect), jailbreaks, RAG and memory poisoning, tool abuse, and MCP and multi-agent attack surfaces emerged, and how defenses and benchmarks responded. It stops at attacks and defenses on LLM agents and applications, and leaves out general model robustness, classic adversarial examples and pure privacy attacks.
paper_count_reason: The topic is broad, with six active lineages: injection, jailbreaks, poisoning, tool/MCP/multi-agent, defenses and benchmarks. The pool is large but uneven. 24 papers cover each lineage's founding work, turning points and key successors without minor variants.

lineages.name: Prompt injection and indirect injection attacks
lineages.description: From goal hijacking in GPT-3 apps to indirect injection through retrieved content and adaptive attacks on agent defenses.

lineages.name: Jailbreak attacks and jailbreak defenses
lineages.description: Why safety training fails, optimization-based and automated jailbreaks, and smoothing and prompt-based defenses.

lineages.name: RAG, memory and backdoor poisoning
lineages.description: Corrupting knowledge bases, agent memory or fine-tuning data so that agents follow attacker-chosen content.

lineages.name: Tool abuse, MCP and multi-agent security
lineages.description: Attacks on tool selection, MCP tool descriptions and servers, and injection spreading between communicating agents.

lineages.name: Prompt injection defenses and system-level mitigations
lineages.description: Detection, structured queries, instruction hierarchy, preference-trained models, task alignment and capability-based designs like CaMeL.

lineages.name: Agent security benchmarks
lineages.description: Environments and datasets measuring agent vulnerability to indirect injection and harmful misuse.
